scope: Ten actual saved nativeA states in the first two complete late fixed-gap flights. One frozen native half-step perstate reconstructs exact reaction/phase and next-cortex balances; no trajectory or spatially recentered field is produced.

definitions.distance: direction * shortest signed (rawFV Racphase−fixedgap position). FirstAflightdirection−1,second+1. Times are nearest actual5s snapshots to targets, coordinated with implementation.
definitions.width: TwoR=.8 crossing positions obtained by linear interpolation between native cell centers. Edge positions are reported relative to the rawFVphase for geometry only; native field arrays stay at original coordinates.
definitions.leading: Edge in the measured outgoing direction; trailing is the oppositeedge. Scalar comparisons between flights use these labels rather than reflecting or shifting fields.
definitions.phase_rate: Im(Zdot/Z)/k with exactnativeFV harmonic Z and actualone-stepRacRHS. Components are Rho-inhibitedbasalproduction,MCAdependent/Rho-inhibitedproduction,implicitdecay andsharedFVdiffusion. Rac has noadvection.
definitions.cortex_sources: Exact next-cortex solve at updatedb friction, with oldQ activeforce and newly computed membraneW and Racgapcommands. Current bound transport instead uses old interiorv, so this is not a decomposition of current bound advection.

interpretation: From outgoing distance about2 to10um, firstA activeRac width grows16.258 to21.430um, about31.8%. Vector strength varies nonmonotonically and edgeMCA,Rho andtension change. These measurements contradict rigid translation of a fixed field profile.

The old gap is progressively separated from highRac activity: its trace falls0.89109 to0.82421, smoothprotrusion switch0.16885 to3.15e−7 and maximumcommand0.02502 to4.28e−8um/s. The native mechanicalcut still remains until the separate0.8 connectivity threshold is crossed.

At distance10um, leading-edge next-cortex velocity is supplied almost entirely by Rho active stress (about0.012um/s in the travel direction), while the old-gap command contributes only about7.6e−9um/s in the opposite direction. This is an instantaneous sourceallocation, not an evolved pathwaynecessity result.

OutwardMCA-dependent production contribution falls0.01302 to0.00536um/s, while opposing Rho-inhibitedbasal contribution weakens from−0.01191 to−0.00310um/s. Their changing cancellation allows the netphase speed to rise fromabout0.00109 to0.00222um/s. Fastertravel is not explained by an increasingMCA contribution alone.

The second opposite-directionA flight repeats the selected scalar edge states and geometry closely. A common empirical speed-distance relation can summarize this repeatable prepared trajectory, but distance co-varies with the evolving chemistry,shape andboundaryactuation rather than uniquely controlling the clock.
cautions: Changing activewidth,edgechemistry/tension,rawRacvectorstrength andpoolprofiles contradict rigid translation of a fixed shape. A speed-distance curve can still be a useful descriptive relation along this prepared branch.
The distance and speed co-vary with evolving state; instantaneoussourceallocation doesnot establish a unique causal clockfraction.
Weak gapcommands do not close or remove the mechanicalgap: its displacement/velocity boundary and bounddiffusion interruption remain until the separateRac=.8 lifecycle threshold iscrossed.
The infinitesimal basal growthrate and this finite-amplitude travel are different regimes; no extrapolation or convergence claim is made here.
